title: The largest items adopted without a committee hearing
question: Which files that skipped committee named the most money, and what did each actually do?
finding: 17 files adopted without committee reference since 2019 name $100,000 or more. 4 of them act on the money; the rest schedule a hearing, apply for a grant or take a position on a bill. The largest: Issuance of Revenue Bonds - Public Utilities Commission - Purchase of Electricity Distribution and Transmissio ($3.07 billion, 2020); Supporting California State Assembly Bill No. 1505 (Rodriguez) - $250,000,000 Seismic Retrofitting Program for ($250.0 million, 2023); Committee of the Whole - Loan Agreement - Metropolitan Transportation Commission - Public Transit Operating Pu ($200.0 million, 2026).
how: Every file whose history shows adoption without committee reference and whose short title prints a figure of $100,000 or more, largest figure first. “What it does” is read from the opening words of the title. Each row links to the file.
limits: A bond or grant resolution adopted this way may follow an ordinance or hearing that did go through committee, and the title does not say so; the file’s own history and its related files settle that. Titles that schedule a hearing of the whole Board move no money themselves. The dollar figure is the largest in the title, which for a “not to exceed” authorisation is a ceiling. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
